pr_title: LE Audio: Allow server to initiate Codec Config procedure
pr_body:
Required by ASCS/SR/ACP/BV-07-C PTS test case.

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/46238
pr_comments:
After this refactor the stream has to be configured by the server app before calling the `bt_audio_unicast_server_config_ase()`. The function initializes the selected ASE and configures its codec. Finally, attaches the configured stream to the ASE.

The `bt_audio_unicast_server_foreach_ase()` allows to reach id, state and dir of each ASE, which the server app needs. This approach helped `bt_audio_ep` to stay safe and untouched by external code.

Added example usage of `bt_audio_unicast_server_foreach_ase()` into in the unicast server BSIM test.

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Expose endpoint state to the application
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
It may be useful for the application to know the state of the endpoint associated with a `bt_audio_stream`, instead of the application managing its own state machine based on the stream callbacks. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
One solution to this is to move/copy/reference the endpoint state in the `struct bt_audio_stream`, which is application allocated and thus directly accessible. This is the approach used by ISO and L2CAP. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Another solution is to implement a `bt_audio_stream_get_info` that will return the state, based on the endpoint (if any), which will return a struct containing the state. This is the approach used for `bt_conn`. 

**Additional context**
N/A
comments:
@jhedberg @alwa-nordic @asbjornsabo @MariuszSkamra 

I would like to get some input from you on which approach to take here, since we do not have a general way of exposing internally-changed-only state to the application. 

Should we go the ISO/L2CAP direction, or the ACL direction? 
Should we work on making this more consistent at some point (i.e. either allocate `bt_conn` in the application, or have ISO/L2CAP/Audio have a fixed array of channels of an opaque type that can be requested by the application)? 

This feature was requested by @erikrobstad so pinging him here too.
